title: Gangs of Nightglade - poker based, story driven card battler in CP setting.
author: mlooser_26
selftext:
For the past few months I've been working on this poker-based, story-driven cyberpunk card battler. Last week Steam page finally went live!

You play units into four lanes at once, building poker combos in each (pairs, straights, flushes…), while taking out your opponent's units to break up their sets.

Regarding how it was done and challenges that I had

1. **Art – Codex.** The biggest challenge was keeping the art style consistent. I ended up with a huge markdown file containing a precise style description and references for everything it should be based on. On top of that, I asked Codex for self-review everything it generated against that style guide and **anatomy issues**. 
2. **Code – Claude (Opus).** This part went fairly smoothly, mostly because I have 20+ years of programming experience, so I knew exactly what architecture, patterns and practices I wanted. For example, I wrote the dialogue/quest and gameplay systems for Gwent/Thronebreaker, so I knew precisely what needed to be built and how the game should be structured. The AI was fast hands, not the architect.
3. **Automated testing – the real lifesaver.** I have almost 4k unit tests to keep features stable and make sure Opus doesn’t accidentally break something. For balance, I built a simulation that plays thousands of games and gathers stats, so I can check that no combination of card classes produces an auto-win synergy.
4. **Trailer music – Suno.**
5. **Trailer editing – done manually in DaVinci Resolve.** I tried building it with Opus first, but it was a mess: the cuts just weren’t precise enough.
6. **Unity integration – MCP vs CLI.** I was really disappointed with the Unity MCP. It crashed regularly. Switching to the Unity CLI helped a lot.
7. **Environment art – the trick I’m most proud of.** Getting the right perspective with proper space for the cards was a real struggle. What finally worked: in Unity I drew debug lines showing exactly where the cards would be placed, plus the "perspective lines". I rendered that to a texture, gave it to Codex and asked it to adjust the images to those lines and keep the perspective they marked. That let me produce several environments, all with correct proportions, perspective and card space. I’m really proud of that one.
8. **Still a long way to go.** Despite all my experience and the AI support, after over 100 hours of work I’m far from finished. For example, I’d love to have animated characters in dialogues (like we had in Thronebreaker), but Ludo is sooo random, and I’ve lost a lot of time and credits re-rolling without good results. I’ll probably just rig the sprites and animate them in Unity myself.
9. UI assets - I bought them on Unity Store. It was much simpler that prompting and fixing in PS.



I hope this is useful for someone. If you have any questions, feel free to ask. Happy to help!  
  
Let me know what you think and whether you'd like to play it. Every wishlist means a lot :)
